title: PADA-Coder: Improving Plan-Following Code Generation via Perturbation-Verified Attention Distillation and Dynamic Alignment
claim: Long context makes models over-attend to their own recent output and spread attention too evenly, missing the key constraints.
layout: 2 stacked panels, each heatmap left and schematic right, color-coded headers
description: The figure has two stacked panels, each with a colored title banner. The top panel, "Attention Drift" (peach), shows a lower-triangular attention heatmap in blue shades with a colorbar. Braces label the columns as prompt and code, and the dense diagonal region at the lower right is the code part. To its right, a row of plan steps (step1 to step5) sits above a row of code blocks. A green arrow marks code that correctly attends to step1 at first. A red curved arrow marks drift back to earlier code steps, and a dashed gray arrow marks where attention should go, step5. The bottom panel, "Attention Dispersion" (light blue), shows a near-uniform, mottled code-to-plan sub-matrix heatmap. To its right, a plan token bar has a few green key tokens among pink tokens. A funnel narrows down to a code block, which shows that attention is diffuse.
caption: Observation of Attention Allocation Imbalance. Top (Attention Drift): As sequence length grows, model increasingly attends to the self-generated history (dense lower-triangular region). Bottom (Attention Dispersion): Model distributes attention relatively uniformly, resulting in insufficient focus on key tokens.
abstract: The Plan-then-Code paradigm effectively enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) in complex code generation by decomposing reasoning into explicit, interpretable steps. However, introducing the plan and verification report substantially enlarges the context, which in turn misdirects the model’s attention toward irrelevant tokens and the most recently generated code. This effect leads the model to overlook critical constraints and to generate incorrect code, especially for small-scale LLMs (less than 8B). To address this issue, we propose \textbf{P}erturbation-Verified \textbf{A}ttention \textbf{D}istillation and Dynamic \textbf{A}lignment (PADA). PADA identifies the key tokens most critical to the student model and constructs the optimal attention target matrix, dynamically aligning the student’s focus with key tokens for each plan step. We evaluate PADA with two teacher models and three student models across seven benchmarks, and the results show that PADA improves Pass@1 by up to 16.7\% and outperforms SOTA methods in overall average performance.
